messages.subject: GSoC 2013. Proposal. Discrete choice modeling
parts:
Hello,
I am a PhD student of the Mathematical Methods and Representation
Department at University of A Coru�a.
I started my PhD in Civil Engineer majoring in Transportation in 2010
and my thesis is focused on discrete choice modeling. Since that, I've
been working with R.

Usually, I use the mlogit package [1] for estimate my models on R. This
package use, to do the description of the variables involved in the
model, extended model formulas which are build upon formula objects
provided by the Formula package [2]. However, this are not very
practical for models with advanced utility specification because the
formula object force to have the same variables for all the utility
specification of the alternatives. And the best, for a realistic
representation of choice behaviour, would be that you could be able to
use a different specification for each alternative.

In the scope of the Google Summer of Code I'm very interested in
developing the required methods and functions needed to improve the
mlogit package and fix this limitation.
I think this will allow easily estimate advanced model structures on R,
like other software packages for discrete choice estimation do (e.g.
Biogeme [3]).

If you have other suggestions related with discrete choice modeling I'll
be very happy to discuss about it and see if I could work on it!
I am a linux user and have programming experience with C++, Fortran and
Python. Also, I have a big background on maths (I have a master's degree
in civil engineering).

Thanks,
Ana Mart�nez Pardo
